mini.title: Life Skills
mini.passage: Ovaries contain egg cells; testes produce sperm cells after puberty begins. A pregnancy can begin when a sperm fertilizes an egg, usually in a fallopian tube, and the resulting developing structure implants in the uterus. Puberty does not mean someone is ready to become a parent. Private body parts have correct anatomical names, and questions deserve accurate respectful answers. Grade 7 extension: sexually transmitted infections can spread through sexual contact, sometimes without symptoms. Avoiding sexual contact prevents sexual transmission; correctly used condoms reduce but do not eliminate infection risk. Other birth-control methods do not protect against STIs. A trusted adult or health professional can answer questions.

items.prompt: Which organ supports an implanted developing pregnancy, and which cells can combine in fertilization?
items.answer: The uterus supports an implanted pregnancy; a sperm cell and egg cell can combine in fertilization.

items.prompt: Make a word-to-function matching chart for ovary, testis, sperm, egg, and uterus using only the reading. Grade 7: also distinguish pregnancy prevention from STI prevention using a reliable health source. Use fictional examples; no personal disclosures. Use a labeled drawing and 3-5 sentences.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.
